title: Rapid PR capture cheatsheet
content:
Goal: capture the minimum useful review outcome in <10 minutes so the author can iterate. This is a personal rapid-capture template I've been testing — minimal friction, high signal.

Usage patterns:
- 3-minute triage (first pass): decide whether PR is ready for detailed review or needs quick changes. Use for small changes, hotfixes, and early morning triage.
- 10–20 minute focused read: follow for medium PRs (behavioral changes, config tweaks).
- Deep review (30+): reserve for architecture or surface-area changes.

3-minute triage checklist (literal):
1) Does the title/description explain the user-visible change? Yes/No
2) CI green? quick glance at test results and e2e summary. Pass/Fail
3) Risk level: tiny / small / medium / large (pick one)
4) Rollback complexity: one-liner revert / requires migration revert / unclear
5) Quick blocker? (no tests, secrets, prod-configs) — call out immediately
If any No or blockers -> leave a short inline note + request changes.

Rapid note format I leave under the PR description: (copy/paste)
- Triage: small / needs-work / ready-for-deep
- Quick blockers: <short bullets>
- Suggested next step: (e.g., add unit test, remove debug flag, separate rename)

Core heuristics I use for fast judgments:
- One behavior per PR: if the PR mixes renames + logic change + perf tweak, prefer decomposition.
- Tests should demonstrate regression or behaviour; not just snapshot churn.
- Config changes touching prod defaults require explicit rollout plan.
- Surface-area increases (new public API, new env var) => call out in changelog and add migration notes.

Micro-checklist for refactor follow-ups (use in comment threads):
- Maintain backward compatibility notes (if public)
- Add a small test that would fail before refactor (sanity)
- Preserve observable metrics (latency/call-count) — add a smoke perf check if risky
- Add a TODO linking to a tracking ticket if the refactor defers cleanup

Suggested quick comments to reduce back-and-forth:
- "Small: could you split rename vs logic? I can re-review the latter once split."
- "Tests: please add one unit that asserts X; otherwise behavior is ambiguous."
- "Perf: add a short smoke run in CI (1000 requests) or a note in the PR about expected cost/regressions."

Triage flow for flaky tests / CI failures:
- Look at failure class (unit / integration / e2e). If unit flaky -> rerun; if integration/e2e -> request log + reproduction steps.
- If flaky pattern unrelated to PR file changes, mark flaky and ask infra to investigate, but don’t block author unless it prevents verification.

Quick mental checklist for security/secret risk:
- Any env var or secret loaded directly from repo? flag as urgent.
- New dependency with native bits? ask for SBOM and runtime privileges check.
- Config exposing endpoints/credentials -> require risk owner sign-off.

Examples of minimal inline comments I leave:
- Line 23: "This predicate is O(n) in list length; for 10k inputs might blow memory — is caller bounded?"
- Line 78: "Nit: prefer early return to reduce indentation"
- Line 104: "Behavior change: previously returned nil; now raises. Add migration note or revert to preserve behavior."

Keyboard-friendly micro-workflow (hotkeys + tiny script):
- Open PR -> cmd+f "TODO" -> scan -> x minutes limit timer -> leave triage blurb -> mark as ready/needs work
- Local quick run: ./scripts/run-unit.sh --changed-files --headless (helps verify tests touched by PR)

Quick rubric for accept vs request changes (for PRs < 300 LOC):
- Accept if: CI green, tests covering behavior, low blast radius, clear title/description.
- Request changes if: ambiguous behavior, missing test that verifies a real user-path, production config changes without rollout, or new third-party dep without justification.

Follow-up backlog capture (short form to paste into issue tracker):
- Task: split PR into rename + logic + perf (owner: author, estimate: 1–2d)
- Task: add migration note to docs site (owner: docs, estimate: 2–4h)
- Task: add smoke perf check in CI for endpoint X (owner: infra, estimate: half-day)

Questions to ask the author (one-liners):
- "Why this approach vs X? quick pros/cons?"
- "Is this change user visible? any migration needed?"
- "Can you add a focused test that would detect regression?"

Common shortholds I watch for (patterns that usually need more work):
- Large PRs with many unrelated files changed.
- Tests added but only asserting mocks instead of behavior.
- Silent API behavior changes (return types, error modes).
- Hidden feature flags toggled on by default without rollout plan.

My personal habit: if I spend >15 minutes and still feel fuzzy about intent, I pause and ask for a short walkthrough or a design doc link. That saves multiple rounds.

Quick templates to paste as comments (complete sentences are better):
- "Thanks — quick triage: I'd like a focused unit test for the changed behavior and a short note about rollout. Happy to re-review after."
- "This looks risky: could you split the rename from the logic change? I can approve the rename separately."

Closing notes / reminders to self:
- Keep triage language crisp. The goal is to unblock the author, not be exhaustive on first pass.
- Use follow-up tickets liberally instead of blocking small finish work.
- Update this cheatsheet after a thread where review style caused churn.

----
Scratch area (quick captures):
- PR #4123: needs test that fails on old behaviour (see added example in comment)
- TODO: make a tiny script to capture changed-files unit test run output and attach to PR
- Idea: add a lightweight label "triaged" that includes risk level + blocker quick notes

End of doc.
